page.layout: One page of text. Running head and page number at the top. Margin notes in the right margin beside the verse and the first paragraph of the argument. Catchword at the bottom right.

main_text.p: mni utilitigatione cum Deo abstinere. Nemo enim nostrūm Deo est à confilijs: Roman.11.34.
main_text.head: VERSUS XIIII.

p.i: Facisq; homines similes piscibus maris: similes reptili, cui non est dominator.

main_text.head: 5. ARGUMENTUM, à disparatis.
main_text.p: Antecedens dens.Non eo modo agendum est cum hominibus, quo cum piscibus & reptilibus: nec concedendum, ut homines prępote-tes in cęteros ita posint sæuire, ut solent pisces maiores in minores grassari. Nam, ut præclarè apud Cedrenum Iustinus 2. Imperator loquitur: Si me à Deo putatis Imperatorem factum, eius auxilio imperare, parete iustis meis mandatis, & iniuria afficere pauperes definite. Solis namq; piscibus moris est, ut validior & maior devoret minorem. Quòd si meis præceptis non parere, sed in rapiędo ali-ena uestris obsequi uultis cupiditatibus, alium uobis uestro arbitratu deligite Im-peratorem. Ego enim contumacibus, in-iustis, ac aliena inuolantibus imperare nolo. Pagina Annalium 319.

page.notes: Printed page with running head "IN HABACVC CAP. I." (u/v normalised as "IN HABACUC CAP. I."). Doubtful: the reference "Roman.11.34." (numerals may be "ii" rather than "11"); "rapiędo" (the second vowel/ligature uncertain, perhaps "rapiendo"); the first word "mni" is a fragment, probably the end of "omni"; the margin note "Antecedens" carries a reference sign before it and is set in italic, read here as "Antecedens" with the second line "dens." Long s has been normalised to s throughout. Verse "Facisq;" read as printed.
